acceptance: Execute workflow-equivalent CLI/publish smoke with reviewer pin A and trusted gate pin B; observable gate decision follows B, never imported A.
Gate subprocess failure records retry/failure state and cannot publish a success or silently swallow errors.
Fixture matrix covers new head, same-head rerun, dispute, findings/withdrawals, stand-ins, carry, absence/quota/retry and fork PR secret boundaries with unchanged current semantics.
Cold-run verification installs exact locked bytes and dependencies; candidate build receives no privileged credentials. CI/config checks and independent review pass before merge.
context: T4 offline, P5. First live gate and required-check activation belong exclusively to theseus-gateway-client-first-live-gate-20261102. Actual BenchBox workflow cutover belongs to theseus-atomic-benchbox-cutover-20261102.
description:
Implement Theseus-hosted review/gate workflow contracts and a sandbox consumer path that preserve hosted CI plus local pre-submission operation. Reviewer uses the run's trusted base lock. Publication-time gate resolves the current trusted gated-branch lock into a separate verified process; never load two package pins in one Python interpreter. Surface gate subprocess failures through the existing GitHubError/retry-state path. Candidate checkout and untrusted build jobs get no App, gateway, publisher or production secrets. Explicitly document reusable-workflow caller context, token permission ceilings, environment secret handling and pinned workflow ref. Workflow permissions stay least-privilege.
Guardrails: offline/fake-OMP fixtures only; no new live gateway client, shared configuration change, release publication, credential service, daemon or activation. Do not alter BenchBox workflow behaviour until atomic cutover. Keep protocol and required-check contracts stable and fork gate-path PRs fail-closed.
